reason: The text explicitly demonstrates Yahweh's care for the people of Israel, not merely the leaders. Yahweh directs David to 'shepherd' (רעה) His people Israel, establishing the leader's role as caretaker of the collective. Yahweh grants military victories to protect the people from Philistine invasion and blesses common individuals like Obed-edom and his household, demonstrating empathy extending beyond leaders. Additionally, David distributes gifts to all the people from man to woman, a practice presented approvingly in the narrative. There is no evidence in the text of selective empathy favoring only leaders while lacking it for the general population.
